ojime.sense: noun: A Japanese carved bead worn between the inrō and netsuke.

ojha.sense: noun: A sorcerer or folk healer in parts of India and Nepal.

firstUse.quote: No one ascends the mountain through fear of the demon, except an Ojha or sorcerer, who sacrifices a goat at the foot of the hill before he makes the attempt.
firstUse.source: 1894, William Crooke, An introduction to the popular religion and folklore of northern India, Allahabad, page 36:

ojek.sense: noun: A motorcycle taxi in Indonesia.

firstUse.quote: It empties its perennially clogged streets of ojeks, the kamikaze-like motorcycle taxis that weave in and out of traffic, and find shortcuts on sidewalks.
